messages:
marco: Quick heads-up: onboarding Riptide Pay LoRA merge (cust). Deployed merged weights to staging and ran our finance quick-eval. Noticed consistent spacing/splitting around currency & percent tokens under int4 quant. Can we run a compatibility sweep + quant sanity? cc @anya @oz
anya: link pls and run command?
marco: s3: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/riptide/pay_quickpack_2024-11-12.tar.gz
run we used: `./evaluate_quickpack.sh --model riptide-merged-lora --quant int4 --evalset pay-bill-samples.json --seed 7`
oz: ran a 100-case quick run. pass 88%. Failures concentrated on money/percent fields. Examples in logs:
```
[2024-11-12T09:11:03Z] case=PAY_021 input="Amount: €3,40" output="Amount:  3 . 4 0"
[2024-11-12T09:11:05Z] case=PAY_034 input="Fee: 2.5%" output="Fee: 2 . 5 %"
[2024-11-12T09:11:10Z] case=PAY_068 input="Total USD 120.00" output="Total USD 120"
```
oz: tags: tokenizer=byte-bpe-1.9, quant_profile=int4-fast
sylvie: those look like tokenization+decode-prob shifts. The inserted weird char in first example could be an encoding artifact from our tokenizer mapping under int4 kernel. Did you use the customer's tokenizer bundle or our default?
marco: used customer's tokenizer bundle v1.0.0 that they committed with the LoRA.
eval-bot: quick-eval complete (run=qk-1750129876-1). metrics: exact_match=0.86, numeric_format_score=0.71, halluc_rate=0.02. deltas vs staging-fp16 baseline: numeric_format_score -0.18, token_split_regress +0.11
marco: repro locally: fp16 vs int4 shows gaps. fp16 preserves `€3,40` intact, int4 sometimes inserts spaces or splits digits.
anya: possible causes: 1) tokenizer mapping differences between customer's bundle and our runtime tokenizer table; 2) quant noise causing softmax jitter around punctuation tokens; 3) decoding temperature/beam interplay. quick checks: run int4 with greedy and beam=1, and run int4 with per-channel quant + clip.
devnull-bot: Note: when evaluating customer-sensitive numeric data, consider enabling numeric-normalizer postprocess (opt-in) to avoid false positives in automated regressions.
sylvie: immediate mitigation: repack with our canonical tokenizer v1.2.0 (we fixed the mapping for euro comma variants), and try the int4-calibrated profile with 3% outlier clip and per-channel symmetric quant. Can anya prepare a repack?
anya: yes. I'll rebase tokenizer to v1.2.0 and build int4-calib (clip=3.0) profile, push new quickpack tonight, and kick off a 1k-case smoke against the dedicated test pool tomorrow.
oz: please include a small synthetic set that stresses comma vs dot decimals (EUR, locale variants) and percent-edgecases. I'll add ~120 synthetic cases to the evalset.
eval-bot: Scheduled full run after new quickpack upload (will post results here).
marco: thanks. Also let's add a short note to the customer handoff doc: customers with money/receipts workloads should prefer fp16 or validated int4-calib profiles; we should surface that in the Console as a warning when a model/tag contains currency-heavy examples.
anya: noted. Will include the recommendation and the quickpack artifacts in the upload.
sylvie: FYI tagging for triage: severity=low (customer not blocked), impact=billing-format, owner=@anya, followup=tokenizer-pin+quant-calib.
marco: I'll post the repack link when ready and mark this thread resolved after the 1k smoke passes. Appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:
